espn_all.name: Hunter Long
espn_all.short: Long (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Commanders, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.
espn_all.long: The tight end returned from injured reserve two weeks ago and has two grabs for 18 yards on three targets in two games since suffering a knee injury. Long is now dealing with an ankle issue. Teagan Quitoriano would see an uptick in snaps behind Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins if Long is unable to play.

espn_all.name: Jeremiyah Love
espn_all.short: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Friday that he has no update on Love (ankle), who is eligible to come off injured reserve following Sunday's game against the Commanders, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.
espn_all.long: Love will miss a fourth consecutive game Sunday but will then be eligible to come off injured reserve ahead of Week 13 against the Eagles. LaFleur previously said Love will be reevaluated Monday once eligible to return, and the coach added Friday that he expects to know more Wednesday once the Cardinals return to practice. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight are still the leading in-house backfield options in the meantime.

espn_all.short: Beck (back) will not play Sunday against the Commanders, coach Mike LaFleur said Friday, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.
espn_all.long: Beck has yet to resume practicing and will miss a second consecutive game Sunday due to back spasms, paving the way for Josh Johnson to start against Washington. LaFleur added that a Week 13 return against the Eagles is in play for Beck, who made his first regular-season NFL start in a 34-6 Week 10 loss to the Rams. Beck's practice participation level leading up to that game will provide an indication regarding his potential availability, and LaFleur added that the team will know more about Beck's status "early in the week," per Weinfuss.

espn_all.long: Bowman was unable to participate in practice all week due to a hamstring injury that will sideline the second-year defensive back for the fourth time in the Falcons' last five games. Sydney Brown will operate in an elevated role in the secondary in the absence of Bowman, whose next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Lions on Sunday, Dec. 6.

espn_all.name: Zachariah Branch
espn_all.short: Branch (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Minnesota, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
espn_all.long: Branch will join Jahan Dotson (hamstring) on the sidelines in Week 12. Drake London, Olamide Zaccheaus, Beaux Collins and Chris Blair are Atlanta's available options at wide receiver, while Zaccheaus and Khalil Herbert are the top candidates to handle punt and kickoff returns in Branch's absence. Branch's next opportunity to suit up will be Sunday, Dec. 6, against Detroit.

espn_all.long: Dotson hasn't practiced all week, so it wouldn't be surprising if he's ultimately ruled out for Sunday's game against the Vikings once the Falcons release game designations Friday. Zachariah Branch (hamstring) also remained sidelined at Friday's practice, so Olamide Zaccheaus, Beaux Collins and Chris Blair may be Atlanta's only healthy and available wide receivers behind Drake London against Minnesota.

espn_all.name: Nnamdi Madubuike
espn_all.short: Madubuike (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Houston, Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site reports.
espn_all.long: Madubuike is set to miss a second consecutive game due to a hamstring injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Chargers. With the Ravens on a bye for Week 13, the seventh-year defensive lineman's next opportunity to play is Week 14 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Dec. 13. Broderick Washington and Aeneas Peebles are both in line for more rotational snaps on the defensive line in Madubuike's absence.

espn_all.name: Jaylinn Hawkins
espn_all.short: Hawkins (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Texans, Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site reports.
espn_all.long: Hawkins' absence will extend to six games due to a knee injury that he sustained in a practice session during Week 7 prep. The Ravens are on a bye for Week 13, so perhaps the extra rest will be enough for Hawkins to be cleared to return for Week 14 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Dec. 13.

espn_all.long: Franks popped up on the Panthers' injury report with a wrist injury Thursday, and now there's a cloud over his status for Week 12. He may end up taking an injury designation into gameday if he's not able to upgrade to full participation at practice Saturday.

espn_all.name: Bobby Okereke
espn_all.short: Okereke (foot) did not participate at practice Friday.
espn_all.long: Okereke has been sidelined for the Panthers' last three games because of a foot injury, and his availability for Week 12 is now in doubt. Unless he's able to return to practice Saturday, it's not likely he'll be able to suit up Monday against the Buccaneers.

espn_all.name: Mitchell Evans
espn_all.short: Evans (Achilles) was a limited participant at practice Friday.
espn_all.long: Evans took a step in the right direction by practicing to some extent Friday after being listed as non-participant on Thursday's estimate. He'll have one more chance to reach full participation Saturday ahead of Monday's game against the Buccaneers. Evans had his best game of 2026 in the Week 11 win over Baltimore, catching all five of his targets for 44 yards and his first touchdown of the season.

espn_all.name: Tommy Tremble
espn_all.short: Tremble (knee) remained a limited participant at practice Friday.
espn_all.long: Tremble was limited again Friday after being listed a limited participant on Thursday's practice estimate. He has one more opportunity to upgrade to full participation Saturday, which could help Tremble avoid an injury designation for Monday's game against the Buccaneers.

espn_all.name: Jonathon Brooks
espn_all.short: Brooks (groin) practiced without limitations Friday.
espn_all.long: Brooks has shed any practice limitations, but he'll still need to be added back to the active roster to play Monday in Tampa Bay. Even if Brooks gets the green light to suit up and is activated by the Panthers, he'll likely have to settle for a change-of-pace role behind Chuba Hubbard against Tampa Bay's excellent run defense.

espn_all.name: Darren Waller
espn_all.short: Waller (knee) practiced in a limited fashion Friday.
espn_all.long: Waller was among four Panthers tight ends to have a capped session Friday, the others being Tommy Tremble (knee), Mitchell Evans (Achilles) and Feleipe Franks (wrist). Waller was able to play through his knee injury this past Sunday against the Ravens, when he handled a 46 percent snap share en route to three catches (on three targets) for 42 yards.

espn_all.name: Tetairoa McMillan
espn_all.short: McMillan (foot) was not in uniform for the team stretch portion of Friday's practice, but he did suit up afterward, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
espn_all.long: Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reported earlier Friday that McMillan was in a helmet and pads, and although he ditched them while stretching he put them back on shortly afterward. Ultimately, Friday's injury report will include McMillan's activity level, if any, after he was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's practice estimate due to a sore foot.

espn_all.long: Incoom was placed on injured reserve in late October due to a calf injury that he sustained in Week 6 against the Eagles. Regardless of his practice participation over the next three days, the Panthers would have to activate Incoom from injured reserve in order for him to be available for Monday's NFC South tilt against the Buccaneers.

espn_all.name: Brady Christensen
espn_all.short: Christensen (hamstring) reverted to season-ending injured reserve after his 21-day practice window closed Tuesday, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
espn_all.long: Christensen has been rehabbing from a hamstring injury all year, but he was not activated from IR within 21 days of returning to practice, so he'll now miss the rest of the season. The veteran guard will now have to look forward to hopefully returning at some point in 2027.

espn_all.name: Jaycee Horn
espn_all.short: Horn is progressing well in his recovery from a quadriceps injury, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
espn_all.long: Horn is currently considered day-to-day, but head coach Dave Canales wants to ensure Horn is in a great head space before returning. The 2021 first-round pick has been sidelined since late September, while Chau Smith-Wade has handled slot-cornerback duties in his absence. The Panthers will still have to officially activate Horn off injured reserve before he's eligible to return.

espn_all.name: Colston Loveland
espn_all.short: Loveland (knee) is slated to get a second opinion on his knee injury and won't be placed on injured reserve for now, though he is considered week-to-week, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
espn_all.long: Schefter reported earlier that the Bears planned to place Loveland on injured reserve due to the knee injury the TE sustained in Thursday's 39-35 win over the Lions, which would rule Loveland out for at least four games. Chicago wants to gather more information before a determination is made on Loveland's status, and the door is still open for a shorter absence, though it would be surprising at this point if he's able to play Sunday, Dec. 6, against the Jaguars.

espn_all.name: Caleb Williams
espn_all.short: Williams said after Thursday's 39-35 win in Detroit that he's "fine" and likely just has "a bruise on his abdomen," Jason Lieser of the Chicago Sun-Times reports.
espn_all.long: Williams seemingly went for a precautionary X-ray after Week 12 action due to a "weird fall" that occurred during Thursday's contest in which he engineered two TD drives in the final 8:20 of the fourth quarter to eke out a four-point victory. He completed 30 of 44 passes for 345 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions and recorded three carries for 15 yards. With plenty of time to recover before the Bears' next game Sunday, Dec. 6 against the Jaguars, Williams has a decent chance to avoid practice restrictions next week.

espn_all.short: Keenum (coach's decision) is inactive and tabbed as the Bears' emergency third quarterback Thursday in Detroit.
espn_all.long: Keenum will fill the Bears' emergency quarterback role for a sixth consecutive week. He'll be able to enter Thursday's contest only if both Caleb Williams and Tyson Bagent have to exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

espn_all.short: Johnson (ankle) has been ruled out  for Thursday's game against the Lions.
espn_all.long: Johnson injured his ankle in Sunday's win over the Saints, and with the quick turnaround for Week 12, he won't be available against the Lions. The Bears will roll with D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai as their only healthy backs for Thursday's game.

espn_all.name: Andrei Iosivas
espn_all.short: Iosivas (thumb) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints.
espn_all.long: Iosivas had his 21-day window to return from IR opened Nov. 12, so the Bengals are running out of time to add him back to the active roster before he would need to miss the remainder of the season. If Iosivas isn't activated ahead of Sunday's game, expect such a move to transpire early the following week before the Bengals travel to Cleveland. Dohnte Meyers has been filling in as Cincinnati's No. 3 WR during Iosivas' ongoing absence.

espn_all.name: Tee Higgins
espn_all.short: After not practicing Friday, Higgins (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
espn_all.long: Higgins wasn't on the Bengals' Week 12 injury report until Friday, but after missing the team's final practice, the wideout's status is now worth tracking ahead of Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff. While a late-week downgrade in practice participation like this can't be ignored, Ben Baby of ESPN.com notes that "Higgins just woke up with some soreness" Friday and that the team gave the WR "the day to work through it." More importantly, Baby indicates that the issue isn't a concern in terms of Higgins' availability versus New Orleans.

espn_all.long: Davis strung together multiple full practices since being designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 12, but he still drew the doubtful tag for Monday's game. He'll end up missing a seventh consecutive game due to a hamstring injury, and his next chance to return is Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday.

espn_all.name: Oren Burks
espn_all.short: The Bengals placed Burks (groin) on injured reserve Saturday.
espn_all.long: Burks has been working through a groin issue for the past couple of weeks, and he aggravated the injury during the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday. His placement on IR means he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Panthers on Sunday, Dec. 20.

espn_all.name: Raheim Sanders

Even if Sanders gets the green light, he's unlikely to see much action on offense, with Quinshon Judkins, Dylan Sampson and Jaleel McLaughlin all healthy in Cleveland's backfield.

espn_all.name: Jaishawn Barham
espn_all.short: Barham (hip/groin) does not carry an injury designation into Thursday's game against the Eagles.
espn_all.long: Hip and groin injuries prevented Barham from playing in Week 11 against the Titans, but his full session Wednesday was enough for him to avoid a designation for Thanksgiving Day. The rookie third-rounder has accumulated 37 tackles (21 solo) and one forced fumble through 10 regular-season games.

espn_all.name: P.J. Locke
espn_all.short: Locke (concussion) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against Philadelphia.
espn_all.long: Locke entered the league's concussion protocol following the Cowboys' Week 9 win over the Colts. He hasn't progressed enough in his recovery to return for Thanksgiving Day and will thus miss a third consecutive game. Locke's next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Seahawks on Monday, Dec. 7.

espn_all.name: Jonathan Mingo
espn_all.short: Mingo (ankle) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Eagles.
espn_all.long: Mingo's absence for Thanksgiving Day will be his third missed game in a row due to an ankle injury that he sustained in Week 9 against the Colts. His absence means KaVontae Turpin and Camden Brown will continue to operate in rotational roles on offense behind CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy. Mingo's next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Seahawks on Monday, Dec. 7.

espn_all.name: DaRon Bland
espn_all.short: Bland (ankle) is expected to return this season, Calvin Watkins of  The Dallas Morning News reports.
espn_all.long: Bland was placed on injured reserve Sunday after suffering an ankle injury during the Week 10 loss to the 49ers, but the injury is not expected to be season-ending. The earliest Bland will be eligible to make his return is the Week 16 matchup versus Jacksonville, and Ameer Speed and Cobie Durant should continue to see increased playing time in his absence.

espn_all.name: Caleb Lohner
espn_all.short: Lohner (foot) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Steelers.
espn_all.long: Lohner was a full participant in all three practice sessions during Week 12 prep. However, the second-year pro is not quite ready to be activated from injured reserve, so his next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6. Lohner is in the final stages of his recovery from a procedure on his foot in June.

espn_all.name: J.K. Dobbins
espn_all.short: The Broncos placed Dobbins on the reserve/suspended list Wednesday, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
espn_all.long: Head coach Sean Payton had previously announced Tuesday that Dobbins would be suspended for Friday's game against the Steelers due to conduct detrimental to the team, but it wasn't immediately clear whether or not the running back would count toward the 53-man roster. As a result of Wednesday's transaction, the Broncos will now have an open roster spot to use for Week 12, and Tyler Badie (thumb) could be activated from injured reserve to help fill the void in the backfield. Dobbins' suspension came after he played just one snap in the Broncos' 38-24 win over the Raiders on Sunday, when rookie Jonah Coleman took on a bell-cow role and handled 28 touches.

espn_all.name: Jonah Elliss
espn_all.short: Elliss (ankle) did not participate in Tuesday's practice and is unlikely to be designated to return from injured reserve ahead of Friday's game against the Steelers, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
espn_all.long: Tuesday was Denver's first practice, and given Elliss's absence, he's highly unlikely to participate in any of the Broncos' next two sessions ahead of Black Friday. The third-year linebacker is recovering from an ankle injury that landed him on IR in late October. Assuming he doesn't play in Week 12, Elliss's next opportunity to play would be Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6.

espn_all.name: DJ Wonnum
espn_all.short: Wonnum (back) is inactive for Thursday's Week 12 battle against the Bears.
espn_all.long: Wonnum was able to practice in a limited capacity Wednesday, but that didn't end up being enough for him to suit up Thursday. He leads the Lions with 7.0 sacks this season, so the veteran defensive end's absence is a big deal for Detroit. Tyler Lacy, Ahmed Hassanein, Eric O'Neill and Anthony Lucas could all be involved in trying to fill the void left by Wonnum's absence Thursday.

espn_all.name: Chuck Clark

espn_all.long: Clark dealt with a hamstring issue during Week 12 prep and is going to miss his first game of the campaign as a result. He's been a starter at safety for the Lions all season and played every defensive snap in three of Detroit's past four games. Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch will start at safety Thursday, with Andre Cisco working in reserve.

espn_all.long: Prior to leaving, the linebacker recorded four tackles (two solo). Dani Dennis-Sutton and Brenton Cox will see an uptick in snaps off the edge for Green Bay.

espn_all.name: Christian Watson
espn_all.short: Watson (concussion) has been ruled out for the rest of Wednesday's game against the Rams.
espn_all.long: The wideout hasn't cleared concussion checks and will miss the remainder of the Week 12 contest after he was injured at the end of the second quarter when Watson took a hit to the head from Kamren Kinchens. Look for J. Michael Sturdivant and Bo Melton to see increased snaps alongside Matthew Golden and Savion Williams with Watson sidelined.

However, the veteran linebacker will end up missing a fifth consecutive game due to a hairline fracture in his shin that he suffered during a practice session in late October, so Ty'Ron Hopper will continue to operate in an elevated role on defense. Franklin's next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Saints on Sunday, Dec. 6.

espn_all.short: Jacobs (finger) is listed as inactive Wednesday at the Rams, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
espn_all.long: Coming out of the Packers' Week 11 bye, head coach Matt LaFleur told Matt Schneidman of The Athletic on Saturday that he didn't expect Jacobs to play in Week 12, but he also gave the running back a "chance to prove" he can. Jacobs then was listed as limited on practice reports Sunday through Tuesday and tagged as questionable ahead of Wednesday's game. Such activity wasn't enough for Jacobs to get the all clear to suit up, meaning Green Bay's backfield will be manned by Kaleb Johnson, MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks for a second consecutive contest.

espn_all.name: Luke Musgrave
espn_all.short: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Saturday that he doesn't anticipate Musgrove (neck) returning from the PUP list this season, according to NFL reporter Jason B. Hirschhorn.
espn_all.long: LaFleur acknowledged that Musgrove is still in the process of rehabbing the neck injury he sustained during OTAs in June, and the Packers haven't yet prepared for the tight end to resume practicing. Barring dramatic progress in his recovery over the next month, Musgrave looks like he'll be sidelined for the final season of his rookie deal before hitting free agency in the spring.

espn_all.name: Danielle Hunter

espn_all.name: Drake Maye
espn_all.short: For now, Maye -- who suffered a fractured right fibula during a Week 10 loss to the Lions -- remains on the Patriots' 53-man roster rather than injured reserve, with coach Mike Vrabel citing the "balance" the team is hoping to strike with regard to managing its remaining designated to return from IR slots, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
espn_all.long: Per Reiss, teams are limited to eight players that can be designated to return from the list over the course of the regular season, and the Patriots are close to using them all. "Right now, he's not on injured reserve," Vrabel said Monday. "He's on the active roster, so that's where it is today. I think that those things are obviously fluid. But we want to try to give him every opportunity that we can to be back at some point in time. I don't know when that will be; I'm not sure. But also, try to manage the roster and do what we need to do to try to win each week." On Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that Maye was on track to miss at least six weeks, a timetable that suggests, in a best-case scenario, the QB could make a push for a late-season return or for the postseason, should New England qualify. Heading into a Week 12 game against the Chargers, Tommy DeVito is slated to work as the team's starter, with rookie Behren Morton on hand as his backup. Additionally, there's the possibility that the team considers Daniel Jones -- who the Colts let go Friday -- as an alternative, but Vrabel told Reiss that in the short term at least, adding another signal-caller is not something that's being planned.

espn_all.name: Shelby Harris
espn_all.short: Harris (illness) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Colts.
espn_all.long: Harris was battling an illness that prevented him practicing during Week 12 prep, and he's not progressed enough in his recovery to play in Sunday's contest. Darius Alexander and CJ Okoye are both in line for more rotational snaps on the defensive line in the absence of Harris, whose next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the 49ers on Sunday, Dec. 6.

espn_all.name: Greg Newsome II
espn_all.short: The Giants placed Newsome (ankle) on injured reserve Tuesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
espn_all.long: Newsome is expected to undergo surgery for a sprained ankle that he sustained in the Giants' 23-18 win over the Jaguars on Sunday. Now that he's on IR, Newsome will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 16 against the Lions on Monday, Dec. 28. Paulson Adebo is expected to start opposite Deonte Banks at outside cornerback in Newsome's absence.

espn_all.name: T'Vondre Sweat
espn_all.short: Sweat (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
espn_all.long: The defensive tackle remains on injured reserve after having his 21-day practice window opened Wednesday, but he's been full in practice and appears to have a decent chance at being activated Saturday and playing Sunday. Sweat hasn't played since Week 7.

espn_all.name: Omar Cooper Jr.
espn_all.short: Head coach Aaron Glenn announced Friday that Cooper (ankle/groin) will remain out for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
espn_all.long: Cooper will miss a second consecutive game Sunday, bringing him up to six total absences as a result of ankle injuries during his rookie campaign. Adonai Mitchell is set to start on the outside opposite Garrett Wilson, with Isaiah Williams manning the slot, though another elevation for practice-squad WR Sterling Shepard could be on the table after Shepard scored twice in the Week 11 win over the Chargers. Cooper's next chance to play will be a Week 14 home game against the Broncos following the Jets' Week 13 bye. Glenn said the timing of the bye played into the decision to keep Cooper out Sunday, per Rich Cimini of ESPN.com, which suggests Cooper has a decent chance to return after the bye.

espn_all.name: Harrison Phillips
espn_all.short: Phillips (ankle) was listed as a limited participant in the Jets' practice estimate Thursday.
espn_all.long: Phillips upgraded to limited participation after sitting out Wednesday's practice, and he also managed to play through the ankle injury during the Week 11 win over the Chargers. Jack Heflin would be in line for increased playing time during Sunday's matchup against the Dolphins if Phillips ends up being unable to play.

espn_all.name: David Onyemata
espn_all.short: Onyemata (abdomen) was estimated as a full practice participant on Wednesday's report.
espn_all.long: Onyemata was designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 18 but was not cleared to play against the Chargers in Week 11. If he can string together full practices over the next two days, then Onyemata would have a good chance of being activated from IR ahead of Sunday's AFC East tilt against the Dolphins.

espn_all.name: DeVonta Smith
espn_all.short: Smith (back) was seen limping badly in the locker room after Thursday's 39-38 win over the Cowboys, Martin Frank of the Delaware News Journal reports.
espn_all.long: Smith put together a career stat line during the Eagles' Thanksgiving Day win, with the veteran wide receiver hauling in 11 of 14 targets for 200 yards and two touchdowns. He was in and out of the game after landing hard on his tailbone on one of his targets in the fourth quarter and was in noticeable pain when on the field. Smith will have additional time to rest courtesy of the Thursday game, but his status over the coming days will be worth monitoring ahead of the Eagles' Week 13 road tilt against the Cardinals on Sunday, Dec. 6.

espn_all.name: Dallas Goedert
espn_all.short: Goedert (shoulder) had his right arm in a sling following Thursday's 39-38 victory over the Cowboys, Jimmy Kempski of PhillyVoice.com reports.
espn_all.long: Goedert injured his right shoulder during the first half of Thursday's game and was not cleared to return. He'll undergo further tests to determine the severity of the injury, but the veteran tight end is certainly in jeopardy of not being available for the Eagles' Week 13 road tilt against the Cardinals on Sunday, Dec. 6. Johnny Mundt, Zach Ertz and rookie second-rounder Eli Stowers would all be in line for larger roles on offense if Goedert were to miss time.

espn_all.name: Gabe Hall
espn_all.short: Hall (wrist) is questionable to return to the Eagles' matchup against the Cowboys on Sunday.
espn_all.long: Hall exited the game in the second half, casting doubt on his availability for the remainder of the contest. Ty Robinson could see an uptick in playing time if Hall ends up being unable to return.

espn_all.name: Marcus Epps
espn_all.short: Epps (foot) has been ruled out for the remainder of Philadelphia's matchup versus the Cowboys on Thursday, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
espn_all.long: Epps is done for the day after suffering a foot injury in the third quarter. In his absence, Kenny Moore has taken over at safety.

espn_all.name: Saquon Barkley
espn_all.short: Barkley suffered a stinger during Thursday's game in Dallas.
espn_all.long: This marks Barkley's second diagnosed stinger of the campaign, but on the previous occasion in Week 2 against the Titans, he was able to check back in to the contest. The Eagles may opt to exercise caution with Barkley, however, because he tended to a neck issue on a short week following this past Sunday's win against the Steelers.

espn_all.name: Cooper DeJean
espn_all.short: DeJean has entered the league's concussion protocol and has been ruled out for the rest of Thursday's game against the Cowboys.
espn_all.long: DeJean was shaken up on the Eagles' first defensive drive of the first quarter and was taken to the locker room, where medical staff diagnosed the third-year defensive back with a concussion. Michael Carter should see more defensive snaps in the secondary in the absence of DeJean, who will now work through the league's protocol in an effort to be available for Week 13 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Dec. 6.

espn_all.name: Cole Payton
espn_all.short: Payton (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game at Dallas but is available as the Eagles' emergency third quarterback.
espn_all.long: Payton will only take the field in Week 12 if starter Joe Milton and backup Tanner McKee leave the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

espn_all.name: Arnold Ebiketie
espn_all.short: Ebiketie (oblique) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Cowboys.
espn_all.long: After his trade to the Bengals fell through two weeks ago, Ebiketie is now dealing with an injury that will sideline him for at least one contest. Jalyx Hunt and A.J. Epenesa should soak up extra snaps off the edge for the Eagles.

espn_all.name: Jonathan Jones
espn_all.short: Jones (ankle) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Cowboys.
espn_all.long: The cornerback was injured in last Sunday's win over the Steelers. With Jones set to miss Thanksgiving Day against Dallas, Riq Woolen and Kelee Ringo are likely to see increased snaps opposite Quinyon Mitchell.

espn_all.name: Brandin Echols
espn_all.short: Echols (quadriceps) has been ruled out for the rest of Friday's game against the Broncos, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports.
espn_all.long: Echols recorded one assisted tackle before leaving the game due to a quad injury that is severe enough for him to not return to Friday's contest. His absence means the Steelers will have less depth both on special teams and in the secondary the rest of the way.

espn_all.name: Jack Sawyer
espn_all.short: Sawyer (knee) has been ruled out for the rest of Friday's game against the Broncos, Burt Lauten of the Steelers' official site reports.
espn_all.long: Sawyer tweaked his knee on the final play of the first quarter, and medical staff have determined that the second-year edge rusher's injury is severe enough for him to not return to Friday's contest. With Sawyer done for the day and Alex Highsmith (ankle) inactive, more defensive snaps are available for Nick Herbig and KJ Henry.

espn_all.name: Cole Holcomb
espn_all.short: Holcomb (heel) is inactive Friday against the Broncos.
espn_all.long: Holcomb will sit out Friday's game after popping up on Thursday's injury report with a heel injury. His next chance to suit up will come Dec. 6 against the Texans. Carson Bruener and Jacoby Windmon could get more run as rotational inside linebackers in Holcomb's absence.

espn_all.name: Kaden Wetjen
espn_all.short: Wetjen (coach's decision) is inactive Friday against the Broncos.
espn_all.long: With Wetjen scratched, Max Hurleman is next in line to return kickoffs and punts on special teams. Hurleman is one of five active wide receivers for the Steelers on Friday, joining DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman, Germie Bernard and Roman Wilson.

espn_all.name: Drew Allar
espn_all.short: Allar (coach's decision) is inactive for Friday's game against the Broncos but will serve as Pittsburgh's emergency third QB.
espn_all.long: Following Aaron Rodgers' departure from Pittsburgh, Allar moves up to the third spot on the depth chart behind Friday's starter Mason Rudolph and Will Howard. Despite the incremental progress, it would take injuries, illnesses and/or ejections to both Rudolph and Howard for Allar to get into Week 12 game action.

espn_all.name: Gennings Dunker
espn_all.short: Dunker (knee) has been ruled out for Pittsburgh's matchup versus the Broncos on Friday,
espn_all.long: Dunker managed to return to practice for the first time since suffering a knee injury in September but will have to wait at least another week before making his return. The rookie sixth-round pick should provide additional depth at guard once healthy.

espn_all.name: Alex Highsmith
espn_all.short: Highsmith (ankle) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Broncos, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
espn_all.long: Highsmith was held out of practice all week due to an ankle injury that he picked up during the Steelers' 19-16 loss to the Eagles this past Sunday, when he logged 2.0 sacks and forced a fumble before his exit. Nick Herbig and Jack Sawyer are the top candidates to start opposite T.J. Watt at the edge rusher position in the absence of Highsmith, whose next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Texans on Sunday, Dec. 6.

espn_all.name: Ben Skowronek
espn_all.short: The Steelers placed Skowronek (calf) on injured reserve Thursday, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
espn_all.long: Skowronek has been working through a calf issue since mid-October, and he appeared to aggravate the injury during the Steelers' Week 11 loss to the Eagles. Now that he's on injured reserve, Skowronek will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 16 against the Panthers on Sunday, Dec. 27. Max Hurleman was signed off the practice squad to the 53-man roster in a corresponding move.

espn_all.name: Jordan Watkins
espn_all.short: Watkins (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
espn_all.long: Warkins was held out of practice all week due to a groin injury, and the second-year wide receiver will end up missing his third game of the season and first since Week 2 against the Dolphins. Keenan Allen, Jacob Cowing and Demarcus Robinson are all candidates for more offensive snaps Sunday in the absence of Watkins, whose next chance to play is Week 13 against the Giants on Sunday, Dec. 6.

espn_all.name: Mike Evans
espn_all.short: Evans (Achilles) is listed as questionable for Sunday's contest against the Seahawks, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
espn_all.long: Evans didn't practice Wednesday before he was listed as limited on Thursday's injury report as he continues to deal with the right Achilles tendinitis that forced him out of a Week 6 matchup with the Commanders. He returned to action this past Sunday versus the Vikings in Mexico City and gathered in six of seven targets for 109 yards and one touchdown on a 43 percent snap share. Evans' status will be clarified about 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff.

espn_all.name: Brock Purdy
espn_all.short: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Friday that Purdy (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game versus the Seahawks, Jennifer Lee Chan of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
espn_all.long: Purdy wasn't able to practice during Week 12 prep due to an ankle injury, which will sideline him for the first time this season. In place of Purdy, Mac Jones will earn the spot start Sunday, while the former's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 6, at the Giants. Shanahan added that surgery isn't on the table for Purdy and he's optimistic the QB will be OK to return in Week 13, according to Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com.

espn_all.name: Austen Pleasants
espn_all.short: The 49ers designated Pleasants (knee) to return from injured reserve Wednesday, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
espn_all.long: Pleasants opened the regular season on injured reserve due to a knee injury that he sustained in a preseason game against the Chargers in late August. He was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, and he would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Seahawks. With Colton McKivitz (ankle) out for the rest of the season, Pleasants would be a candidate to start at right tackle once he's removed from IR.

espn_all.name: Colton McKivitz
espn_all.short: McKivitz (ankle) was placed on the 49ers' injured reserve list Wednesday.
espn_all.long: McKivitz was diagnosed with a fractured and dislocated ankle that he sustained in the 49ers' Week 11 win over the Vikings. He's expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season, and Vederian Lowe is expected to take over as the starter at right tackle in McKivitz's absence.

espn_all.name: Dre Greenlaw
espn_all.short: Greenlaw (neck) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
espn_all.long: Greenlaw was not cleared by medical staff to play against the Vikings in Week 11 due to a neck issue. He's opened Week 12 prep with a limited practice, and a full session over the next two days would likely be enough for him to avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Seahawks.

espn_all.long: questionable

espn_all.name: Sam Okuayinonu
espn_all.short: Okuayinonu (foot) was spotted walking without a limp in the 49ers' locker room Wednesday, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.
espn_all.long: Okuayinonu suffered a broken foot in practice ahead of Week 1 and required surgery. He appears to be making progress and could return at some point before the end of the regular season. The 28-year-old appeared in 15 regular-season games last season, and made 12 starts and recorded 23 tackles (16 solo), including 3.0 sacks, and a forced fumble.

espn_all.name: De'Zhaun Stribling
espn_all.short: San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan said Wednesday that Stribling (ankle) is likely at least "a couple weeks away" from returning to practice, Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reports. "I don't know. I mean, nothing's changed," Shanahan said, regarding a timeline for the rookie receiver.
espn_all.long: Stribling was diagnosed with a deltoid sprain of his left ankle after getting injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams in Australia and underwent surgery Sept. 16. The 23-year-old was handed an estimated recovery timeline of about 10 weeks, leaving the 49ers optimistic that he would be ready to play at some point in December. While Shanahan indicated that Stribling's timeline doesn't appear to have changed, the young wideout will need to get back on the practice field before the 49ers can hone in on a more precise target date for him to resume playing. Given the haziness of his return date along with the fact that he could face limitations with his snaps once activated, Stribling likely isn't worth holding in redraft leagues at this point in the season.

espn_all.name: Jarran Reed
espn_all.short: out
espn_all.long: out

espn_all.name: Quenton Nelson
espn_all.short: Head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters Wednesday that Nelson (knee) will not play against the 49ers on Sunday, Brady Henderson of ESPN.com reports.
espn_all.long: Nelson underwent a minor procedure on his knee in early November and will be sidelined for a second consecutive game. He's had additional time to rest thanks to the Seahawks' Week 11 bye, and Macdonald relayed Wednesday that the team is "hopeful" that Nelson will be cleared to return for Week 13 against the Cowboys on Monday, Dec. 7. Greg Zabel will likely start at left guard in Nelson's absence.

espn_all.name: Abraham Lucas
espn_all.short: Lucas (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Brady Henderson of ESPN.com reports.
espn_all.long: Per John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site, head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters Wednesday that Lucas is not a candidate for injured reserve but is expected to miss "days to weeks" due to an ankle sprain that he suffered in Week 10 against the Raiders. Josh Jones, Bobby Hart and Chase Lundt are all candidates to start at right tackle for as long as Lucas is sidelined.

espn_all.name: George Holani
espn_all.short: The Seahawks placed Holani (knee) on injured reserve Monday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
espn_all.long: Holani was knocked out of the Seahawks' last game in Week 10 at Las Vegas due to a knee injury that eventually was deemed to be an MCL sprain. Per Brady Henderson of ESPN.com, head coach Mike Macdonald said he was uncertain if Holani will require surgery, but the running back will be sidelined for at least four games by virtue of landing on IR. In the meantime, Emanuel Wilson will serve as the team's No. 3 back behind Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price.

espn_all.name: Benjamin Morrison
espn_all.short: Morrison (hamstring) did not practice Friday.
espn_all.long: Morrison has been a DNP for each of the first two practices of Week 12 prep due to a hamstring injury that he sustained in Week 11 against the Lions. He would likely need to log at least a limited practice Saturday to have a realistic shot at suiting up for Monday's NFC South showdown against the Panthers.

espn_all.name: Antoine Winfield Jr.
espn_all.short: Winfield (ankle) did not participate in Friday's practice.
espn_all.long: Winfield has been listed as a DNP for each of the first two practices of Week 12 prep due to an ankle injury that he sustained in Week 9 against the Bears. He did not play against Detroit in Week 11, so he would likely have to log at least a limited practice Saturday to have a realistic chance of suiting up Monday against Carolina.

espn_all.name: Josiah Trotter
espn_all.short: Trotter (oblique) was a limited participant in Friday's practice.
espn_all.long: Trotter has opened the week with back-to-back limited practices while recovering from an oblique injury, which he may have picked up during the Buccaneers' Week 11 loss to the Lions. He'll have one more opportunity to log a full practice and avoid an injury designation ahead of Monday's game against Carolina.

espn_all.name: Tez Johnson
espn_all.short: Johnson did not participate in Friday's practice due to an illness.
espn_all.long: Johnson wasn't listed on Thursday's report, so the illness is a recent development for the second-year wide receiver. His participation in Saturday's practice will provide clarity on his status heading into Monday's game against the Panthers.

espn_all.name: Jalen McMillan
espn_all.short: McMillan (knee/calf) was limited at Friday's practice.
espn_all.long: McMillan hasn't played since Week 3 due to a PCL sprain in his left knee, but since he was designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, he was listed as full with knee and calf issues on Thursday's estimated injury report before Friday's downgrade in activity. Ultimately, Saturday's practice report will determine McMillan's chances to return to action Monday against the Panthers.

espn_all.name: SirVocea Dennis
espn_all.short: questionable
espn_all.long: questionable

espn_all.name: Christian Rozeboom
espn_all.short: The Buccaneers opened the 21-day practice window for Rozeboom (finger) on Wednesday, Scott Smith of the team's official site reports.
espn_all.long: Rozeboom has been on injured reserve for the Buccaneers' last four games while recovering from a finger injury that he sustained in late October. Tampa Bay's first practice of Week 12 prep is Thursday, so Rozeboom's participation over those three sessions will determine whether he's recovered enough to be activated from IR ahead of Monday's game against the Panthers.

espn_all.name: Elijah Simmons
espn_all.short: Simmons is in concussion protocol following Sunday's loss to the Lions, Brianna Dix of the Buccaneers' official site reports.
espn_all.long: Simmons played 17 defensive snaps in Sunday's loss but did not appear in the box score. The defensive tackle has now entered the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist to return to full-contact football activities.

espn_all.name: Cor'Dale Flott
espn_all.short: Flott (neck) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jaguars, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
espn_all.long: Flott picked up a neck injury during the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys in Week 11. He was not cleared to practice during Week 12 prep, and in his absence, Micah Robinson figures to start opposite Joshua Williams for Sunday's AFC South showdown. Flott's next chance to suit up is Week 13 against the Commanders on Sunday, Dec. 6.

espn_all.name: Terrell Burgess
espn_all.short: out
espn_all.long: out

espn_all.name: Amik Robertson
espn_all.short: Robertson (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, John Keim of ESPN.com reports.
espn_all.long: Robertson will end up missing a second consecutive game due to an ankle injury that he sustained during the final practice of Week 11 prep, and his absence means Quan Martin will once again operate in an elevated role in the Commanders' secondary. Robertson's next chance to play is Week 13 against the Titans on Sunday, Dec. 6.

espn_all.name: Laremy Tunsil
espn_all.short: Tunsil (triceps) is progressing well in his recovery but is not expected to return by the end of the 2026 regular season, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports.
espn_all.long: Tunsil underwent surgery in August to repair a torn triceps. The left tackle continues to recover, but he likely will not suit up for the Commanders in 2026 unless the team makes a playoff run. Even then, it remains unclear whether Tunsil would be able to return at all before the 2027 season.

feed.headline: The knee injury that Loveland sustained during Thursday's 39-35 win over the Lions is expected to land him on IR, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
feed.description: The knee injury that Loveland sustained during Thursday's 39-35 win over the Lions is expected to land him on IR, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
feed.story: If that's the case, Loveland would need to miss at least four games, with Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network noting Friday that a knee sprain is the initial diagnosis for Loveland. In that scenario, a late-season return could be in the cards for him. In Loveland's anticipated absence, Sam Roush is in line to see added snaps and targets, a context that could yield fantasy relevance down the stretch for the 2026 third-rounder.

feed.headline: Loveland (knee) is scheduled to undergo an MRI on Friday on the knee injury he sustained during Thursday's 39-35 win over the Lions, Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network reports.
feed.description: Loveland (knee) is scheduled to undergo an MRI on Friday on the knee injury he sustained during Thursday's 39-35 win over the Lions, Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network reports.
feed.story: The Bears are hoping the results of Friday's MRI reveal a sprain rather than a tear, as the former outcome could lead to a relatively swift recovery, while the latter scenario could result in Loveland missing the rest of the season. Loveland got hurt in the first half of Thursday's comeback win. Prior to the injury, Loveland caught his only target for five yards but fumbled at the end of that play.

feed.headline: Loveland (knee) has been ruled out from returning to Thursday's game in Detroit.
feed.description: Loveland (knee) has been ruled out from returning to Thursday's game in Detroit.
feed.story: After Loveland was rolled up on in the middle of the first quarter, he was favoring his left knee as made his way to the sideline, where he visited the sideline tent before being carted to the locker room. Now that he officially won't return to this Week 12 contest, rookie third-round pick Sam Roush and veteran Stephen Carlson are the team's healthy and available tight ends.

feed.headline: Loveland (undisclosed) went to the medical tent during Thursday's game at Detroit, Sean Hammond of the Chicago Tribune reports.
feed.description: Loveland (undisclosed) went to the medical tent during Thursday's game at Detroit, Sean Hammond of the Chicago Tribune reports.
feed.story: Loveland limped off the field in the middle of the first quarter and immediately went to the sideline tent. The nature of his injury isn't known, but he had one catch (on one target) for five yards and lost a fumble prior to his exit.
